Much how game consoles do this with 900p, you can get a smooth 60fps gameplay on games that would normally have fps drops here and there without sacrificing widescreen.

To do this, go to Intel HD control panel>Display>and on the left, you should see "custom resolutions." There will be a disclaimer about "overloading your chipset" but we're not overclocking, it will not put more strain on your chipset, so it is totally safe.

To find good resolutions, open a calculator and do width*height of your display to find total pixels for native. If you get drops to 30fps, you will want about half of the pixels. Then use a 16:9 calculator (I used this one http://size43.com/jqueryVideoTool.html ) to get resolutions using estimates of width and use the calculator again to compare gpu strain.

Then in Intel control panel, when entering width and height, be sure to leave the last digit as a ZERO (so instead of 1064x600 , type 1060x600) otherwise it will be an invalid number. Obviously set refresh rate to 60, and click save.

Afterwards games should show these resolutions in the game settings, so no weird game setup required (usually)

For Black Mesa on an Intel 4400, I run at 1000x560, and there are absolutely no times the fps will go below 60 under the GPU bottleneck (CPU can make it go to about 55 sometimes)

My current custom resolutions are (performance boost multiplier based on 1366x768):

680x380 (4x) 856x480 (2.55x) 1000x560 (1.87x) 1064x600 (1.64x)

Hope this works for when you're on the go and can't access your gaming PC at home :)
[protip] If you have an ultrabook, use custom resolutions (for Intel cards)
